controlled_change: Fixed requested width four versus one; identical native producer, full-replay recovery, 1460 target slots, 32 draft slots and 12GiB admission.
correctness: All ten full-model numerical cases pass cleanly. Two fresh alternating timing pairs per workload match all logits, tokens and final target/draft state, with zero compression/decompression and unchanged system swap.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: Lower complete generation-cycle latency with maintained draft state.
hypothesis: The LRU benefit from width one might generalize to interval merging.
limitations: Two pairs per workload have no confidence bound.
128 output tokens after a short prompt do not qualify 2K/4K context, append latency, 7K or sustained coding.
This is a retrospective ledger interpretation, not a newly preregistered test.
outcome: Width four measured 4.3393 and 4.3394 tokens/s; width one measured 4.0537 and 3.8906. Candidate/control geometric latency ratio 1.09268144, or 9.27% higher latency. Both pairs favor width four. This rejects a universal width-one default for the tested suite.
smallest_experiment: Retain width four for profiling this measured workload. Do not repeat a universal width-one switch unchanged.
